title: Removing configurability of `Jenkins.agentProtocols`
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator should not have to manually curate the list of built-in inbound agent protocols in the global security screen, because that configuration can drift away from the supported transport set and create confusion about what Jenkins actually allows.


  ## Desired outcome

  Jenkins should stop treating built-in agent protocols as an administrator-managed security setting and should instead expose the supported protocol set directly from core. The configuration UI and backing APIs should no longer offer agent protocol toggles that imply these built-in transports can be selectively disabled there.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The global security configuration no longer presents agent protocol selection as an editable admin setting, Jenkins reports the supported built-in protocols from core without relying on saved UI state, and upgrading preserves working agent connectivity without a manual protocol reconfiguration step.

  '

title: Simplify AtomicFileWriter and use clearer temporary file names
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator writing critical configuration files expects atomic writes to stay dependable and the resulting logs to be readable when the filesystem does not support true atomic moves, but the current implementation produces obscure temporary names and noisy duplicate failure reporting.


  ## Desired outcome

  `AtomicFileWriter` should create clearer temporary file names derived from the destination path and should remember after the first `AtomicMoveNotSupportedException` that the platform requires a non-atomic fallback. Once that fallback is known, Jenkins should replace the target cleanly without repeating the unsupported atomic attempt on every write.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Temporary files are easier to identify from their names, the first unsupported atomic move downgrades subsequent writes to the non-atomic replacement path, and operators no longer see duplicate stack traces caused by retry-and-rethrow logic when the filesystem lacks atomic move support.

  '

title: '[JENKINS-37241] Support for query parameters in autocomplete'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator or plugin author exposing an autocomplete field may need extra query parameters to scope the results, but the current autocomplete widget only sends the search term and makes it impossible to express that richer filtering contract.


  ## Desired outcome

  Autocomplete endpoints should be able to declare additional query parameters through the descriptor contract, and the browser widget should include them when fetching suggestions. This should let server-side autocomplete logic honor contextual filters without changing the visible widget behavior for fields that do not need extra parameters.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Autocomplete requests include any descriptor-defined extra query parameters alongside the typed term, existing fields without extra parameters keep working as before, and filtered suggestion endpoints can finally distinguish context that was previously unavailable to them.

  '

===== agent-protocols-config-removal.yaml =====
title: Removing configurability of `Jenkins.agentProtocols`
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator should not have to manually curate the list of built-in inbound agent protocols in the global security screen, because that configuration can drift away from the supported transport set and create confusion about what Jenkins actually allows.


  ## Desired outcome

  Jenkins should stop treating built-in agent protocols as an administrator-managed security setting and should instead expose the supported protocol set directly from core. The configuration UI and backing APIs should no longer offer agent protocol toggles that imply these built-in transports can be selectively disabled there.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The global security configuration no longer presents agent protocol selection as an editable admin setting, Jenkins reports the supported built-in protocols from core without relying on saved UI state, and upgrading preserves working agent connectivity without a manual protocol reconfiguration step.

  '

===== atomicfilewriter-temp-names.yaml =====
title: Simplify AtomicFileWriter and use clearer temporary file names
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator writing critical configuration files expects atomic writes to stay dependable and the resulting logs to be readable when the filesystem does not support true atomic moves, but the current implementation produces obscure temporary names and noisy duplicate failure reporting.


  ## Desired outcome

  `AtomicFileWriter` should create clearer temporary file names derived from the destination path and should remember after the first `AtomicMoveNotSupportedException` that the platform requires a non-atomic fallback. Once that fallback is known, Jenkins should replace the target cleanly without repeating the unsupported atomic attempt on every write.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Temporary files are easier to identify from their names, the first unsupported atomic move downgrades subsequent writes to the non-atomic replacement path, and operators no longer see duplicate stack traces caused by retry-and-rethrow logic when the filesystem lacks atomic move support.

  '

===== autocomplete-query-parameters.yaml =====
title: '[JENKINS-37241] Support for query parameters in autocomplete'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator or plugin author exposing an autocomplete field may need extra query parameters to scope the results, but the current autocomplete widget only sends the search term and makes it impossible to express that richer filtering contract.


  ## Desired outcome

  Autocomplete endpoints should be able to declare additional query parameters through the descriptor contract, and the browser widget should include them when fetching suggestions. This should let server-side autocomplete logic honor contextual filters without changing the visible widget behavior for fields that do not need extra parameters.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Autocomplete requests include any descriptor-defined extra query parameters alongside the typed term, existing fields without extra parameters keep working as before, and filtered suggestion endpoints can finally distinguish context that was previously unavailable to them.

  '

===== autocomplete-suggestion-count.yaml =====
title: Allow plugins to customize number of suggestions in autocomplete
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins need far more or far fewer autocomplete suggestions than Jenkins’s hard-coded default, but today they cannot express that preference in the rendered control.


  ## Desired outcome


  Plugin authors should be able to set the maximum suggestion count per autocomplete field without forking the widget.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget still defaults to 10 suggestions when nothing is specified, but a field can override that limit through the `data-maxsuggestions` attribute.

  '

===== background-discarder-logging.yaml =====
title: '[JENKINS-73692] Turn off logging from `BackgroundGlobalBuildDiscarder`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Background global build discarder maintenance can produce noisy per-job logging even when it is working normally, which makes administrative logs harder to scan.


  ## Desired outcome


  Keep the discarder behavior the same while removing routine chatter from its listener output.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The build discarder still evaluates jobs and applies matching retention strategies, but it no longer prints per-job progress lines for every processed job.

  '

===== boot-version-logging.yaml =====
title: Print Jenkins version on boot
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator starting or upgrading a controller often needs to confirm from the startup logs exactly which Jenkins version is coming up, but boot logs do not currently state that version explicitly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When Jenkins starts, the normal startup log should include the controller version so administrators can confirm the running build without inferring it from package metadata or the UI. The boot message should clearly report the value returned by `Jenkins.getVersion()`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Startup logs include a message containing the current Jenkins version during initialization, operators can confirm the running version from boot output alone, and no extra manual step is required to verify which release started.

  '

===== build-deletion-lts-backport.yaml =====
title: Backporting for 2.479.1 (part 3)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator using build deletion, log rotation, or global build discarders expects running builds to be preserved until they have actually finished writing logs, but Jenkins can still try to delete a build while it is running or invoke discarding logic at the wrong point in finalization.


  ## Desired outcome

  Attempts to delete a running build must fail cleanly instead of partially removing it, with the user-visible message `Unable to delete <job> #<build> because it is still running`. Build discarding should run after finalization in a way that respects `isLogUpdated()`, avoids double-running job-level rotation, and only removes builds once Jenkins considers them finished.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Manual deletion of an active build is rejected with the exact `Unable to delete <job> #<build> because it is still running` message, log rotation skips builds whose logs are still being updated, and finalized builds are discarded once without duplicate job-level rotation passes.

  '

===== buildhistory-refresh-all-pages.yaml =====
title: '[JENKINS-73613] refresh buildhistory widget in all cases'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  The build history widget only refreshes reliably on the first page of results, so users looking at older pages can miss renamed builds, description changes, deletions, or updated running-build state until they manually reload.


  ## Desired outcome


  Build history should refresh whenever the page becomes active again and should keep the user on the same slice of history instead of snapping back to the top.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget refreshes on window focus, updates while viewing older pages, and preserves the current pagination context when reloading the build list.

  '

===== build-number-assigner.yaml =====
title: '`Job.BuildNumberAssigner`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Some Jenkins distributions and plugins need to customize how build numbers are allocated, but today the core logic is hard-wired inside `Job`.


  ## Desired outcome


  Expose a supported extension point for build-number assignment while still allowing the implementation to persist the next build number through a controlled callback.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `Job.BuildNumberAssigner` can supply the allocation strategy, `SaveNextBuildNumber` gives that strategy a way to persist the sequence, and the default Jenkins behavior remains the built-in fallback.

  '

===== command-palette-header-guard.yaml =====
title: '`headerCommandPaletteButton` undefined when `JenkinsHeader` not loaded'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins page that does not render the standard `JenkinsHeader` should still be allowed to load frontend assets safely, but the Command Palette initializer currently assumes the header button exists and crashes on layouts that omit it.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette frontend should detect when `headerCommandPaletteButton` is absent and simply skip initialization on that page. Pages without `JenkinsHeader` should remain fully usable instead of failing because the palette tried to bind to a missing control.


  ## Acceptance signals

  On layouts without the standard header, the page loads without JavaScript errors, the palette code exits early when `headerCommandPaletteButton` is missing, and pages that do include the header keep the normal Command Palette behavior.

  '

title: Refine Command Palette UI
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user opening the Command Palette expects it to feel responsive and polished, but the current dialog can show awkward loading flicker, abrupt closing behavior, and visual rough edges that make the interaction feel unfinished.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette should load results with smoother spinner timing, cleaner open-and-close animation, and more consistent spacing and visual treatment so it feels like a first-class navigation surface. The interface should preserve existing search behavior while improving the perceived responsiveness of searching and dismissing the palette.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The loading spinner appears only when searches take long enough to warrant it, closing the palette uses a deliberate transition instead of an abrupt disappearance, and the updated palette styling reads as a polished UI refinement rather than a functional regression.

  '

title: Add icons to Command Palette
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user searching from the Command Palette needs enough visual context to distinguish jobs, users, views, agents, and other results at a glance, but the current results list is text-only and forces people to infer the target type from the name alone.


  ## Desired outcome

  Search results returned to the Command Palette should include both an `icon` and a `type` so the frontend can render the right symbol for each result class. Jobs should expose meaningful status-based icons, and the palette should present those icons consistently across the different result types Jenkins exports.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Command Palette result payloads include `icon` and `type`, jobs surface a status-derived search icon, and users can visually distinguish result categories in the palette without opening each match first.

  '

title: Add icons to Command Palette
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user searching from the Command Palette needs enough visual context to distinguish jobs, users, views, agents, and other results at a glance, but the current results list is text-only and forces people to infer the target type from the name alone.


  ## Desired outcome

  Search results returned to the Command Palette should include both an `icon` and a `type` so the frontend can render the right symbol for each result class. Jobs should expose meaningful status-based icons, and the palette should present those icons consistently across the different result types Jenkins exports.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Command Palette result payloads include `icon` and `type`, jobs surface a status-derived search icon, and users can visually distinguish result categories in the palette without opening each match first.

  '

===== command-palette-ui-refinement.yaml =====
title: Refine Command Palette UI
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user opening the Command Palette expects it to feel responsive and polished, but the current dialog can show awkward loading flicker, abrupt closing behavior, and visual rough edges that make the interaction feel unfinished.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette should load results with smoother spinner timing, cleaner open-and-close animation, and more consistent spacing and visual treatment so it feels like a first-class navigation surface. The interface should preserve existing search behavior while improving the perceived responsiveness of searching and dismissing the palette.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The loading spinner appears only when searches take long enough to warrant it, closing the palette uses a deliberate transition instead of an abrupt disappearance, and the updated palette styling reads as a polished UI refinement rather than a functional regression.

  '

title: '[JENKINS-73785] Restore `ContextMenu#from` with `StaplerRequest`/`Response` args'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins and adjunct code still call the older `ContextMenu#from` overload that accepts `StaplerRequest` and `StaplerResponse`, and that compatibility path disappeared during the newer request-type migration.


  ## Desired outcome


  Restore the legacy overload so existing integrations continue to build and run while the ecosystem migrates to the new request types.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `ContextMenu#from(ModelObjectWithContextMenu, StaplerRequest, StaplerResponse)` is available again and delegates to the newer request and response implementation instead of forcing every caller to migrate immediately.

  '

title: '[JENKINS-73539] Disable YUI by default'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator upgrading the UI stack should get the YUI-free experience by default, because keeping the legacy library enabled unless someone opts in slows the transition and leaves obsolete dependencies active longer than necessary.


  ## Desired outcome

  The `RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag` should default to enabled so Jenkins removes YUI from pages unless an administrator explicitly opts back out through the `jenkins.model.experimentalflags.RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag.defaultValue` system property. Pages that no longer rely on YUI, including the old debug log reader hook, should continue to load without that library being initialized.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Fresh and upgraded controllers default to the YUI-removed path, administrators can still override the default with the `jenkins.model.experimentalflags.RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag.defaultValue` system property, and pages no longer initialize the legacy YUI debug log reader by default.

  '

  Keep a compatibility overload for the old safe-restart signature while steering new development toward the `StaplerRequest2` form.

category: other

  The deprecated `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest)` and `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` entry points should remain tolerant of `null` and forward that call through to the modern restart path without crashing. ===== fips-password-length-validation.yaml =====
title: '[JENKINS-74858]  Added validation for Password length in FIPS mode'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator running with FIPS-compliant cryptography expects local user creation and password changes to reject passwords that are too short for that mode, but Jenkins currently allows values that should not be accepted under the stricter policy.


  ## Desired outcome

  When FIPS mode is enabled, HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm should reject passwords shorter than 14 characters during account creation and password updates, while still allowing valid matching passwords that meet the minimum. The validation should attach to the password field so users understand what must be corrected.


  ## Acceptance signals

  In FIPS mode, passwords under 14 characters are rejected, matching passwords of 14 or more characters succeed, and administrators no longer end up with locally managed credentials that violate the active compliance policy.

  '

===== idiomatic-python-style.yaml =====
title: Follow idiomatic Python coding style
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  The small Python maintenance script in this repository does not follow the project’s current Python style, which makes future edits noisier than they need to be.


  ## Desired outcome


  Align the script with idiomatic Python naming and environment checks without changing what the tool does.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The script behaves the same as before, but contributors see standard Python-style names and CI detection logic when they maintain it.

  '

===== inbound-agent-websocket-default.yaml =====
title: Add -webSocket option by default when creating an inbound agent
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  The Jenkins UI still generates inbound agent launch commands that omit WebSocket mode unless the user notices and adds it manually, even though WebSocket is the safer default for many modern installations and reverse-proxy setups.


  ## Desired outcome


  The generated inbound-agent command should include WebSocket mode by default so new agents start with the recommended connection mode.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The launch snippet produced for an inbound agent includes `-webSocket` even when the user has not toggled an extra option.

  '

===== keyboard-scroll-selection.yaml =====
title: Fix scrolling with keyboard
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user navigating Command Palette results with the keyboard expects arrow-key movement to keep the selected item visible, but the current scroll helper can miss cases where the selected element is undefined and keyboard navigation becomes unreliable.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keyboard-driven navigation should tolerate the absence of a selected item and only try to scroll when a real selection exists. The Command Palette should continue to wire keyboard handling only while it is open so arrow-key navigation stays smooth instead of tripping over an uninitialized selection.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Using the keyboard to move through Command Palette results no longer throws or stalls when nothing is selected yet, scrolling resumes once an item is actually selected, and navigation remains scoped to the palette while it is open.

  '

===== npm-lint-autofix.yaml =====
title: '[JENKINS-73744] npm scripts lint:fix do not work '
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins contributors cannot rely on `npm` autofix commands from the repository root right now, which slows frontend maintenance and creates confusion about the supported workflow.


  ## Desired outcome


  The lint and formatting toolchain should work from the top-level project layout so `npm` scripts like `lint:fix` behave predictably.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Running the repository’s frontend fix scripts from the root uses the relocated configuration and package metadata successfully instead of failing because the tooling still expects the old subdirectory layout.

  '

===== offline-api-since-annotations.yaml =====
title: Fill in since annotations
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Jenkins core and plugin maintainers rely on `@since` metadata to understand when public offline-state APIs became available, especially when adopting newer agent-state contracts across weekly and LTS lines. Missing version tags make those contracts harder to use safely.


  ## Desired outcome

  The public offline-state APIs introduced with the newer computer model should advertise accurate availability information, including `Computer.setOfflineCause(OfflineCause)`, `IOfflineCause`, and `IComputer.getOfflineCause()` as available since `2.483`. This is documentation-quality cleanup, not a behavior change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Source and generated Javadoc show `@since 2.483` on the touched offline-state APIs, plugin developers can tell when those contracts became available without consulting release notes, and runtime behavior remains unchanged.

  '

===== offline-by-design-ui.yaml =====
title: Display appropriate GUI that accurately displays offline by design
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator looking at an agent that is offline by design needs the UI to distinguish between an intentional pause, a user-requested temporary disconnect, and a genuinely offline machine, but the current computer pages and exported state collapse those cases into the wrong icons and messages.


  ## Desired outcome

  Computers that are offline because they are intentionally not accepting tasks should expose that state through the newer `IComputer` and `IOfflineCause` contracts, including the ability to set an offline reason on a never-connected computer with `setOfflineCause(OfflineCause cause)`. The UI and exported search data should then show the correct iconography and reason text for user-disconnected agents versus agents that are simply offline by design.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Agents that are paused or not accepting tasks show distinct visual treatment from disconnected agents, `IComputer.getOfflineCause()` and `IOfflineCause` provide the offline-by-design details needed by the UI, and administrators no longer see a never-connected or intentionally paused agent presented as if it had unexpectedly gone offline.

  '

===== offline-status-persistence.yaml =====
title: '[JENKINS-30101][JENKINS-30175] Simplify persistence design for temporarily offline status'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  The temporary offline state for an agent currently lives partly on the `Computer`, which makes the status fragile across reconnects, controller restarts, and node reconfiguration even though operators expect that intent to persist with the node itself.


  ## Desired outcome


  Temporary offline state and its message should be owned by the `Node`, while compatibility entry points on `Computer` and the CLI continue to behave as operators expect.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Taking an agent offline through the CLI records an `OfflineCause.ByCLI`, `getTemporaryOfflineCauseReason()` reports the persisted message, existing compatibility setters still work, and a missing target still reports `ERROR: No such agent "never_created" exists.`.

  '

===== os-eol-warning-date.yaml =====
title: '[JENKINS-73845] Fix OperatingSystemEndOfLifeAdminMonitor endOfLifeDate displayed on first warning day'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator who sees the operating-system end-of-life warning on the very first day it should appear expects the banner to report the real end-of-life date immediately, but the monitor can show the wrong value on that first warning day.


  ## Desired outcome

  `OperatingSystemEndOfLifeAdminMonitor` should activate on the first warning day and expose `getEndOfLifeDate()` as the actual configured end-of-life date for the matched operating system, not a placeholder or later-updated value. Administrators should be able to trust the date shown in the warning as soon as the banner first appears.


  ## Acceptance signals

  On the warning start date, the monitor activates for the matching OS, `getEndOfLifeDate()` returns the configured end-of-life date right away, and the banner shows the same date administrators are expected to plan around.

  '

===== peepholepermalink-cache-extension.yaml =====
title: '`PeepholePermalink.Cache`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin developers who customize permalink lookup need a supported way to replace the cache behind `PeepholePermalink`, and Jenkins operators expect nearest-build navigation to keep returning the correct build around gaps created by deleted runs. The current implementation hard-codes the cache and leaves some lookup semantics implicit.


  ## Desired outcome

  `PeepholePermalink` should expose its cache as an extension point through `PeepholePermalink.Cache`, with persisted entries using the existing `id + " " + (build == null ? -1 : build.getNumber())` storage shape so alternate cache implementations remain compatible. At the same time, nearest-build and nearest-old-build resolution should preserve the exact numeric behavior Jenkins expects when build numbers are missing.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Plugins can supply a `PeepholePermalink.Cache` implementation without replacing permalink logic wholesale, persisted cache entries stay compatible with the `id + " " + (build == null ? -1 : build.getNumber())` format, and nearest-build navigation returns the documented builds before and after gaps caused by deletions.

  '
